meta.unit: prices poller round-outcome classification (one classification authority per round outcome) + chain pinned-call per-attempt aggregate
meta.purpose: Task 9 wave 4 brief's mutation requirement: the aggregate-vs-last-error classification (property: the posture is order-independent -- W4M1 restores last-error-wins verbatim, W4M5 shrinks the aggregate to a last-attempt window at the chain layer, W4M6 judges only the first attempt), the any-transport-retains-error arm (W4M2 flips unanimity to any-rejection-wins), the all-rejections-discard arm (W4M3 severs the aggregate consult so every total failure takes the error posture), the chain-layer wiring itself (W4M4 puts the pinned path back on doFrom), and the seam interaction at the rewritten site (W4M7/W4M8: the wave-3 landed-flag dodge re-pinned on both rewritten returns, proving the closed routing law survived the wave-4 edit). Run through the wave-16 committed applier (.superpowers/sdd/wave16-mutations/mutate.py): exactly-one-occurrence asserted per edit, byte-level backups, in-memory restores verified byte-identical. Every touched file is CRLF in the working tree (chain.go/chain_test.go were rewritten CRLF by this wave's edits; core.autocrlf normalizes the committed blobs to LF), so multi-line patterns embed \r\n explicitly.
design_notes: THE POSTURE IS A PROPERTY OF THE OUTAGE, NOT OF THE WALK ORDER. Codex round 3's finding is last-error-wins transposing 'one time authority per verdict': the round's posture depended on whichever endpoint's error the failover rotation happened to surface last, and the deferred routing advance rotated that order every cadence, so a persistent mixed outage alternated discard/error -- resetting the daemon's retryBackoff and blanking step_error on alternating rounds. W4M1/W4M5/W4M6 attack order-independence from three directions (wholesale revert, back-biased window, front-biased window); each must die to a daemon-wrapper streak assertion, not to a compile error.

W4M4 AND W4M5 ARE CHAIN-LAYER MUTANTS AND THE PRICES SUITE ALONE CANNOT SEE THEM, disclosed: the poller tests drive fakePollChain, whose CallAtHashFrom mirrors doFromAttempts' aggregate contract. The killers are the chain package's own per-attempt-outcome tests, which pin the REAL Failover to the contract the fake models -- the same fidelity discipline that made the fake's last-error walk honest in waves 2-3. Both mutants' test commands include ./internal/prices/ anyway so the transcript RECORDS that the prices suite is blind to them (the disclosed seam), rather than leaving it to prose.

W4M7/W4M8 re-pin wave 3's dodge shape on the two returns wave 4 rewrote. The seam is closed law ('the deferred routing advance applies unconditionally to every non-landing round'); re-editing the classification site is exactly the edit shape that could have weakened it, so the landed-flag dodge is re-attacked at both rewritten exits even though W3M3/W3M7 pinned the same law at the pre-rewrite text.

NOT mutation-testable, disclosed: the empty-Attempts guard in allAttemptsRejectedPin (len(walk.Attempts) == 0 fails closed to ERROR) -- doFromAttempts constructs a PinnedCallError only after at least one attempt failed and Dial refuses zero endpoints, so no reachable behavior distinguishes the guard; it is defensive depth against a hand-built aggregate. PinnedCallError.Error()/Unwrap()'s last-error mirroring is pinned by the chain tests' wording assertions rather than mutated separately. The daemon-wrapper harness (harnessBackoff + daemonWorkerHarness) is TEST code mirroring cmd/indexer's stepPriceWorkers/retryBackoff verbatim (cmd/** is out of this wave's scope); mutants attack production code only, and the mirror's fidelity is stated line-by-line in the report.

The wave-3 matrix (t9w3-mutations, 14/14 at 1b89fb5) remains the ground for the seam itself, the per-arm dodges and the liveness ping-pong; wave 4 attacks only what wave 4 changed: WHERE the posture comes from (the aggregate) and WHETHER the rewritten site still cannot dodge the seam.
